title: Portlight: a finite bank, pension and cross-border payment project
author: ito_author
status: author-review-passed; all nine owned files frozen for separate peer and coordinator acceptance
scope: Original integrated institution decision with two dated settlement days, H/F ownership and conversion constraints, credit recovery with prior claims, nonlinear retained bond marks, distinct usable cash and equity tests, bank-to-pension transmission, 18 financed policies, finite physical losses, conditional reverse stress, six unfamiliar transfers, full instructor guide and five-domain 100-point rubric. No closing-chapter lab is relabeled as the project.

opening_and_information_audit.finding: Bank assets 172 H, deposits 140 H, equity 32 H. Pension cash 1 plus bank deposit 12 is 13 against benefits 15, giving a separate 2 H funding deficit. Consolidated bank-pension equity is 30, eliminating the internal 12 claim once.

Sponsor cash 30 funds actual bank subscription b and separate pension grant z; lender cash 20 is separate. Dealer starts with 100 H and 40 F; borrower collateral buyer has 20 H. Bank-owned long bonds secure the line; borrower-owned collateral funds its separate recovery. Dealer and lender budgets are never reused as sponsor resources.

Bill issuer, domestic borrower operating cash and offshore recovery are explicitly stipulated funded external receipts with named payer, currency and arrival date. Conservation is limited to the modeled bank/pension/sponsor/lender/dealer ledgers and collateral proceeds allocation, not a closed whole-economy endowment audit.

Early 09:00 foreign payments precede 10:00 home and 10:15 pension payments. Final 17:00 foreign receipts/payments precede 18:00 home and 18:15 pension payments. These cutoffs are not years. The long bond has a held-fixed two-discount-period remaining-maturity mark q=(1+y)^(-2), does not mature or sell in the horizon, and is distinct from the maturing bill.

Domestic losses 0,6,12 H are recognized once; net collateral 0,10,12 enters actual final receipts 40,42,40. First arrears 0,8,12 and final nominal unpaid 0,6,12 survive writeoff. Foreign unpaid face 0,2,4 F is translated at scenario spot once. Subsequent collection is an asset exchange, not another loss.

Actual payments are capped by cash and outstanding claim in the declared priority. The 2 H reserve is a criterion, not a creditor or an amount withheld during a failing waterfall. Early misses remain historical failures after late cure. Home cash >=2 and marked bank equity >=20 apply only at both home closes; every bank and pension obligation must be on time. No extra F buffer or intraday capital floor is claimed.

Received subscription buys b/(32+b) of residual marked bank equity with limited liability. The sponsor cannot spend the bank stake as bank cash again. Its pension grant is separate and gross b+z is a commitment metric, not welfare or net economic investment cost.

proof_audit.argument: At reference spot, prefunding exchanges equal-valued H/F assets and subscriptions add b. Scenario FX revalues the original net F position 1+f; credit impairment is then charged at the scenario spot. The retained long bonds add 20(q-1), domestic loss and translated foreign loss subtract once, and secured interest 0.05g is the only later expense. Principal payments/collections and currency exchanges at e preserve equity. Hence E_final=32+b+(1+f)(e-2)+20(q-1)-domestic_loss-e*foreign_loss_F-0.05g, including unpaid creditors retained at nominal liability.

Joint early conversion is zero, so 6+f>=15 forces menu f=10. Full benefits require 1+12+z>=15, forcing z=2. Joint pre-loan H is b+8 and reserve plus early H claims is 32; capacity is 20/3, so b>=52/3 forces b=20. All later and capital gates are independently checked, making these necessary conditions sufficient for the original finite menu. Exactly one of 18 candidates qualifies; commitment is 22 H.

For (10,10,2), joint H resources 18 plus capped 20/3 draw pay households 18 and pension 20/3. Pension pays 29/3 and misses 16/3 at the deadline. Late FX 43/9 cures nominal arrears but cannot cure timing; final equity 158/9 remains below 20. Do not add pension lateness again to bank economic loss.

proof_audit.result: Finite VaR and ES with an atom
proof_audit.argument: Selected capital-adjusted losses are 0,127/10,1094/45 with physical masses 1/2,1/3,1/6. Mean 2237/270; CDF reaches 5/6 at 127/10, so lower VaR at 75%=127/10. The worst quarter uses all 1/6 joint mass and only 1/12 credit mass, giving ES at 75%=5519/270. Independent code minimizes t+E[(L-t)+]/(1-alpha) at all loss knots and checks the tail allocation caps; it does not use the author model tail filler as oracle.

With fixed selected policy, requested draw 4 and all other inputs held fixed, reserve feasibility is 15q>=4. On that feasible-draw region final equity is 94/5+20q and the capital floor requires only q>=3/50. Therefore first failure boundary q=4/15, y=sqrt(15)/2-1, with equality feasible and final equity 362/15. Full early creditors can still pay down to q=2/15 after the reserve fails. The fixed draw is not extrapolated below capacity.

Supported yields are [0,4] and corresponding prices [1/25,1]. A positive price boundary inside this domain gets an exact 48-step rational yield bracket and equality execution. Unsupported or zero boundaries get null bracket/equality evidence, not an invented feasible q=0. The normal-only zero-capital transfer exercises this branch.

proof_audit.result: Continuous repair for late conversion cap
proof_audit.argument: With cap 1 F, keeping f=10,z=2 and extra equity 0<=delta<=4 gives draw 4-delta and late H need 4.2-1.05*delta. Available conversion H is 3, so delta>=8/7. Equality repairs all dates/capital; adding grid b=22 is separately selected and recomputed.

Ownership of 20 units is unchanged but eligible units 10 give capacity 10/3. Required draw 4-delta fits iff delta>=2/3; equality cash, conversion and equity are reconstructed. Inaccessibility is not an additional marked market loss.

proof_audit.result: Changed binding constraint from senior recovery
proof_audit.argument: Joint prior claim 9 reduces bank collateral receipt by 6. Feasible-draw equity becomes 64/5+20q; the capital floor q>=9/25 exceeds the collateral floor 4/15. The new yield boundary is 2/3 with E=20 and facility capacity 27/5 greater than draw 4. The original policy still qualifies at original y=1/2.

The explicit Cartesian menu is exhaustive for at most 64 supported policies. Feasibility is a conjunction over every scenario, never probability-weighted. Rank qualifying policies by (b+z,f,b,z). This proves only the chosen finite rule under the original contract, not global welfare optimality, scenario completeness, real delivery or authority.

learner_deliverable_audit.solution_scope: Opening identities, separate external budgets, dates, currency location, title and legal nominal claims fully derived in instructor sections 1 and 4; evidence demands include actual beneficiary credit and funded capacity, not only acknowledgment.

All three states have exact primary-service ratios, net collateral, first/final nominal arrears, impairments and asset-liability bridge. The guide distinguishes principal, interest, impairment, marked values and cash.

Reference model executes all 18 policies in all three states. Selected full journals and all candidates’ dated closes are independently reconstructed. Failed (10,10,2) fully traces funded partial payments and subsequent cure. The learner must implement independently; reference execution alone does not earn that evidence.
Exact mean, quantile, atom-adjusted ES and fixed-policy yield boundary, equality and capital test supplied. The distinction among reserve breach, actual creditor miss and negative equity is explicit.

Illustrative conditional decision specifies evidence, funding, risk bearers, separation of roles, escalation, independent challenge, compensation eligibility and revision. Preferences/control dependence/legal authority are not assumed proven by the procedure. Alternative views are graded by rights, dates and resources.

Required independent code/input/output/source log/manifest/oracles/correction chronology plus six transfer answers and ten-minute oral defense. All twelve chapters are explicitly connected; finite/scenario/rights/mark limits must be defended.

refinements.change: Made the two home-close capital/reserve rules explicit; reserve is a criterion rather than a claimant. Preserved nominal borrower arrears after writeoff. Held remaining long-bond maturity/mark convention fixed. Kept sponsor and lender endowed budgets separate.

limitations: Separate peer/coordinator acceptance and complete-volume integration remain pending; this author record is not the canonical accepted status.
All prices, funding, probabilities, rights and dates are original synthetic contractual inputs; actual external funding, account ownership, delivery and legal authority require evidence outside code.
Long-bond marks are retained unrealized values under a fixed remaining-maturity convention; marked equity is not usable cash.
Pension retained bank claims are reconciled at face, not certified economic default recoveries; borrower legal arrears survive carrying-value writeoff.

Only 18 original policies, three supplied scenarios and a one-factor conditional reverse boundary are certified; no all-path solvency, global crisis optimum, empirical crisis frequency or lifetime pension adequacy is implied.
Debt conversion in transfer 6 is an explicit oral contract alteration, not an implemented hidden switch; meaningful real redesign would require new rights and funding.
No general equilibrium, strategic run, broad stochastic simulation, asset liquidation after secured default or whole-economy endowment audit is claimed.
Author and separate-agent review are not external human certification; no actual reader visual/mobile/keyboard/print QA was performed by this author.
